title: Topic 1.2: Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading

pages.lesson:
LESSON: READING 1.2.1 EXTENSIVE READING: INDEPENDENT READING

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 1.2: Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! Today we learn about Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading. Read the explanation, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: How can you ensure that you benefit from a reading session?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify a variety of texts for independent reading
2. read selected materials for information and enjoyment

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. identify a variety of texts for independent reading
   In simple words: practise until you can identify a variety of texts for independent reading. Use examples from school and home in Kenya.

2. read selected materials for information and enjoyment
   In simple words: practise until you can read selected materials for information and enjoyment. Use examples from school and home in Kenya.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: Talk about Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading using something you see at school in Kenya.

Example 2: Give a home example from your county, estate, or village.

Example 3: Teach a younger child one idea from this lesson in simple words.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Underline two new ideas about Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading in the examples.
2. Explain Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading to a parent using one local example.
3. Draw or write three things that show you understand Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading.
4. Show that you can: identify a variety of texts for independent reading

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading using examples from school or home.
2. Answer: Why is Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading important for a Grade 7 learner?
3. Make a one-minute oral presentation to a parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. Read selected print and non-print materials independently,
2. Respect is developed as learners avoid distracting others by observing good reading habits.

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. identify a variety of texts for independent reading
2. read selected materials for information and enjoyment

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original learner lesson from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
